primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: IPEX syndrome due to hemizygous FOXP3 loss of function causes regulatory T-cell dysfunction and early systemic autoimmunity
mechanism: FOXP3 is a transcription factor required for the development and suppressive function of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells. Hemizygous loss-of-function variants in FOXP3 impair peripheral immune tolerance, producing severe early-onset autoimmunity with enteropathy, eczema, and autoimmune endocrinopathy.
vignette: A 7-month-old boy has chronic watery diarrhea, poor weight gain, severe eczema, and insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus. He has no history of recurrent opportunistic infections. His total T-cell, B-cell, and NK-cell counts are within reference ranges. A maternal uncle died in infancy after a similar illness.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains this patient's findings?
distractor_notes: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome is caused by defective lymphocyte apoptosis, classically with chronic nonmalignant lymphadenopathy/splenomegaly and autoimmune cytopenias rather than the infantile enteropathy-eczema-diabetes triad.

Omenn syndrome is a form of severe combined immunodeficiency with erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, eosinophilia, and marked T-cell dysfunction; normal standard lymphocyte counts alone do not diagnose IPEX, but the autoimmune endocrinopathy-enteropathy pattern is much more characteristic.

Severe combined immunodeficiency causes profound cellular immune dysfunction with severe recurrent/opportunistic infections and abnormal lymphocyte number or function rather than isolated regulatory-T-cell failure causing systemic autoimmunity.
Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome causes eczema, infections, and thrombocytopenia with small platelets; autoimmune diabetes and enteropathy from FOXP3-related Treg dysfunction are not its defining pattern.
key_expl: The combination of male infancy, severe autoimmune enteropathy, eczema, and type 1 diabetes is classic for IPEX syndrome. FOXP3 loss of function disrupts regulatory T-cell development/function while routine T-, B-, and NK-cell enumeration may remain normal.
objective: Recognize IPEX syndrome from early-onset enteropathy, eczema, and autoimmune endocrinopathy in a male infant and connect it to FOXP3-dependent regulatory T-cell dysfunction.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy caused by a pathogenic MYBPC3 sarcomeric protein variant
mechanism: Nonsyndromic familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is commonly caused by autosomal dominant pathogenic variants in sarcomeric genes, particularly MYBPC3 and MYH7. The myocardium develops hypertrophied, disorganized cardiomyocytes with myofiber disarray and interstitial fibrosis, producing impaired relaxation and potential dynamic outflow obstruction.
vignette: A 19-year-old collegiate athlete has exertional presyncope. His father died suddenly at age 34. Echocardiography shows asymmetric interventricular septal hypertrophy without aortic valve disease. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in MYBPC3.
lead: Which myocardial histologic finding is most strongly associated with this disorder?
correct: Hypertrophied cardiomyocytes with myofiber disarray and interstitial fibrosis
distractors: Diffuse replacement of cardiomyocytes by adipose tissue predominantly in the right ventricle
Extensive subendocardial coagulative necrosis with neutrophilic infiltration
Myocyte vacuolization with iron deposition demonstrated by Prussian blue staining
Noncaseating granulomas with multinucleated giant cells
distractor_notes: Fibrofatty replacement of the right ventricular myocardium is characteristic of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy rather than classic sarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Acute coagulative necrosis with neutrophils indicates myocardial infarction and does not explain familial asymmetric septal hypertrophy.
Iron deposition can cause restrictive or dilated cardiomyopathy in iron overload but is not the characteristic histology of MYBPC3-associated HCM.
Noncaseating granulomas suggest cardiac sarcoidosis rather than inherited sarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
key_expl: MYBPC3 is one of the most commonly involved sarcomeric genes in nonsyndromic HCM. The classic microscopic substrate is hypertrophied cardiomyocytes arranged in disorganized bundles, often with interstitial fibrosis.
objective: Connect a familial MYBPC3-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotype to the characteristic histology of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, myofiber disarray, and interstitial fibrosis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency causes liver injury through toxic intracellular accumulation of polymerized abnormal AAT in hepatocytes
mechanism: The common severe Z variant of SERPINA1 causes abnormal alpha-1 antitrypsin folding and polymerization within hepatocytes, impairing secretion. Liver disease is a toxic gain-of-function process from intracellular protein retention, whereas emphysema results from loss of circulating antiprotease activity.
vignette: A 42-year-old man with no alcohol use has chronic elevation of aminotransferases and early panacinar emphysema. Liver biopsy shows periodic acid-Schiff–positive, diastase-resistant cytoplasmic globules in hepatocytes. Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin is markedly decreased.
lead: Which mechanism most directly produces this patient's hepatic injury?
correct: Retention and polymerization of misfolded alpha-1 antitrypsin within hepatocytes
distractors: Unopposed neutrophil elastase digestion of hepatocyte extracellular matrix
Autoantibody-mediated destruction of hepatocyte surface antigens
Failure of copper excretion into bile with lysosomal copper accumulation
Defective canalicular export of conjugated bilirubin
distractor_notes: Unopposed neutrophil elastase is the principal mechanism of the pulmonary emphysema in AAT deficiency, not the hepatocyte injury.
Autoimmune hepatitis is immune mediated and does not explain low serum AAT with PAS-positive diastase-resistant hepatocyte globules.
Defective biliary copper excretion is the mechanism of Wilson disease, which has a different biochemical and histologic pattern.
Defective canalicular conjugated-bilirubin transport causes hereditary conjugated hyperbilirubinemia but does not produce retained AAT polymers.
key_expl: AAT-associated liver disease is caused by abnormal AAT molecules that polymerize and are retained within hepatocytes, a toxic gain-of-function mechanism. The lung disease is mechanistically different: low circulating AAT permits excessive neutrophil elastase activity.
objective: Distinguish the hepatic gain-of-function mechanism of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency from the pulmonary loss-of-function mechanism by recognizing toxic hepatocyte retention of polymerized AAT.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: 5-alpha-reductase type 2 deficiency due to biallelic SRD5A2 variants impairs testosterone-to-DHT conversion
mechanism: SRD5A2 encodes 5-alpha-reductase type 2, which converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone in fetal androgen-responsive tissues. Testosterone supports Wolffian duct differentiation, while DHT is crucial for masculinization of external genitalia and prostate. Affected 46,XY individuals therefore have testes, absent Müllerian structures, preserved male internal ducts, undervirilized external genitalia, and often increased virilization at puberty.
vignette: A 16-year-old adolescent raised female is evaluated for primary amenorrhea and increasing virilization during puberty. Karyotype is 46,XY. Testes are present in the inguinal canals, the uterus is absent, and imaging shows epididymal and vas deferens structures. Serum testosterone rises normally after stimulation, but dihydrotestosterone is low.
distractor_notes: Complete androgen insensitivity causes a 46,XY individual with testes and absent uterus, but functional androgen-receptor failure prevents pubertal virilization despite normal or elevated testosterone and DHT.
17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency impairs sex-steroid synthesis and causes hypertension and hypokalemia; testosterone production would not rise normally.
Persistent Müllerian duct syndrome results from AMH or AMH-receptor defects and therefore preserves Müllerian structures, unlike this patient.
Swyer syndrome is 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis with streak gonads and persistence of Müllerian structures because functional testes do not develop.
key_expl: The preserved Wolffian derivatives show adequate testosterone action, while absent Müllerian structures indicate functioning Sertoli-cell AMH. Low DHT with pubertal virilization and undervirilized external genitalia points to SRD5A2 deficiency.
objective: Differentiate 5-alpha-reductase type 2 deficiency from androgen insensitivity and gonadal dysgenesis using internal reproductive anatomy, testosterone/DHT physiology, and pubertal virilization.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus is promoted by ENaC-mediated lithium entry into collecting-duct principal cells with reduced AQP2 expression
mechanism: Lithium enters collecting-duct principal cells through the apical epithelial sodium channel ENaC. Intracellular lithium interferes with vasopressin-dependent signaling and reduces aquaporin-2 abundance, impairing urinary concentration. Amiloride blocks ENaC and reduces lithium entry, making it mechanistically useful in lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
vignette: A 45-year-old man treated with lithium for bipolar disorder develops polyuria and polydipsia. Serum sodium is mildly elevated. Urine remains dilute after desmopressin administration. A potassium-sparing diuretic is selected specifically because it can reduce lithium entry into the collecting-duct cell type responsible for this disorder.
lead: Which transporter is directly inhibited by this treatment?
correct: Apical epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in collecting-duct principal cells
distractors: Basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase in collecting-duct principal cells
Apical Na+-K+-2Cl− cotransporter in the thick ascending limb
Apical Na+-Cl− cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule
Basolateral sodium-bicarbonate cotransporter in the proximal tubule
distractor_notes: Basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase maintains sodium gradients but is not the amiloride-sensitive entry pathway used by lithium at the apical principal-cell membrane.
NKCC2 is inhibited by loop diuretics and is located in the thick ascending limb rather than being the principal lithium-entry pathway.
NCC is inhibited by thiazides in the distal convoluted tubule; thiazides can reduce polyuria by other mechanisms but do not directly block principal-cell lithium entry.
The proximal basolateral sodium-bicarbonate cotransporter participates in bicarbonate handling and is unrelated to amiloride's protective action against lithium entry.
key_expl: Amiloride inhibits ENaC on the apical membrane of collecting-duct principal cells. ENaC is a major route for lithium entry into these cells; blocking it attenuates lithium-induced AQP2 downregulation and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
objective: Explain why amiloride is mechanistically useful in lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus by linking ENaC blockade to reduced lithium entry into collecting-duct principal cells.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Brown-Séquard syndrome from spinal cord hemisection produces ipsilateral corticospinal/dorsal-column deficits and contralateral pain-temperature loss below the lesion
mechanism: The corticospinal tract and dorsal columns ascend or descend ipsilaterally within the spinal cord after their relevant decussations occur outside the affected segment, whereas spinothalamic pain-temperature fibers cross within a few spinal segments after entry. A hemisection therefore produces ipsilateral upper motor neuron weakness and loss of vibration/proprioception below the lesion with contralateral pain-temperature loss beginning below it.
vignette: A 29-year-old man sustains a penetrating injury involving the left half of the spinal cord at T10. Several days later, he has left-leg spastic weakness and loss of vibration and joint-position sense below the lesion. Pain and temperature sensation are reduced on the right side beginning a few segments below T10.
lead: Which lesion best explains this pattern?
distractors: Complete transverse spinal cord lesion at T10
Central cord lesion affecting the anterior white commissure
distractor_notes: A complete transverse lesion would produce bilateral motor and sensory deficits below the level rather than the crossed hemicord pattern.
A dorsal-column-only lesion would impair ipsilateral vibration and proprioception but would not produce ipsilateral corticospinal weakness or contralateral pain-temperature loss.
A right anterolateral lesion could impair left-sided pain and temperature but would not explain the ipsilateral left pyramidal and dorsal-column deficits.
A central lesion involving the anterior white commissure classically causes segmental bilateral pain-temperature loss rather than this below-level hemisection pattern.
key_expl: This is the classic Brown-Séquard pattern produced by hemisection of the left spinal cord: ipsilateral corticospinal and dorsal-column deficits with contralateral spinothalamic loss below the lesion.
objective: Localize Brown-Séquard syndrome by integrating the spinal-cord trajectories and decussation patterns of the corticospinal, dorsal-column, and spinothalamic systems.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to KRT5 or KRT14 dysfunction causes intraepidermal cleavage within basal keratinocytes
mechanism: Keratin 5 and keratin 14 form the intermediate filament network of basal epidermal keratinocytes. Dominant-negative KRT5/KRT14 variants can weaken the intracellular cytoskeleton so mechanical stress causes cytolysis and blister formation within the basal epidermis rather than at the basement membrane or below it.
vignette: A 4-year-old child has recurrent painful blisters on the palms and soles after friction. Blisters heal without significant scarring. Electron microscopy shows cytolysis within basal keratinocytes, while the basement membrane remains attached to the dermis. Genetic testing identifies a dominant-negative KRT14 variant.
lead: Which cellular structure is primarily defective?
correct: Intermediate filament network of basal keratinocytes
distractors: Anchoring fibrils beneath the lamina densa
Hemidesmosomal laminin-332 linking basal cells to basement membrane
Type IV collagen network within the basal lamina
distractor_notes: Anchoring fibrils are primarily composed of type VII collagen and are defective in dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, where cleavage occurs below the basement membrane.
Laminin-332 defects cause junctional epidermolysis bullosa at the dermal-epidermal junction rather than cytolysis within basal keratinocytes.
Type IV collagen is a basement-membrane structural protein and is not the KRT14-encoded cytoskeletal component.
Desmosomal cadherin defects can cause acantholytic disorders but do not explain KRT14-associated basal keratinocyte fragility.
key_expl: KRT14 encodes keratin 14, which pairs with keratin 5 to form intermediate filaments in basal keratinocytes. EBS from KRT5/KRT14 variants causes mechanical fragility and cleavage within the basal epidermal layer.
objective: Localize the structural defect in keratin-associated epidermolysis bullosa simplex to the basal-keratinocyte intermediate filament network and distinguish it from junctional and dystrophic blistering disorders.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Second branchial cleft cyst results from incomplete obliteration of the cervical sinus and presents as a lateral neck mass along the anterior sternocleidomastoid border
mechanism: The second pharyngeal arch overgrows the third and fourth arches, creating a transient cervical sinus lined by ectoderm. Failure of complete obliteration can leave a second branchial cleft cyst, sinus, or fistula; the cyst classically lies along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid.
vignette: A 17-year-old girl develops a painless, fluctuant lateral neck mass after an upper respiratory infection. The mass is located along the anterior border of the upper sternocleidomastoid muscle. It does not move with tongue protrusion.
lead: Persistence of which embryologic structure most directly accounts for this lesion?
correct: Cervical sinus derived from the second branchial cleft region
distractor_notes: A persistent thyroglossal duct produces a midline neck cyst that typically moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion.
The first pharyngeal pouch forms the auditory tube and middle ear cavity and is not the source of the typical lateral second branchial cleft cyst.
The ultimobranchial body contributes parafollicular C cells to the thyroid and does not form this lateral neck cyst.
The omphalomesenteric duct connects embryonic midgut to the yolk sac and can produce Meckel-related abdominal or umbilical anomalies, not a lateral neck mass.
key_expl: Most branchial cleft cysts arise from incomplete obliteration of the second branchial cleft/cervical sinus. They typically appear as painless lateral neck masses along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, often becoming noticeable after infection.
objective: Identify a second branchial cleft cyst from its lateral neck location and relate it to persistence of the embryonic cervical sinus rather than the thyroglossal duct or pharyngeal pouch derivatives.
clues: does not move with tongue protrusion

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Menkes disease due to ATP7A dysfunction causes impaired cellular copper export/distribution and deficiency of copper-dependent enzymes
mechanism: ATP7A is a P-type copper-transporting ATPase involved in intestinal copper export and intracellular copper trafficking. Loss of ATP7A function causes systemic copper deficiency and impaired activity of copper-dependent enzymes such as lysyl oxidase, dopamine beta-hydroxylase, and cytochrome c oxidase, producing neurodegeneration, connective-tissue abnormalities, and characteristic pili torti hair.
vignette: A 5-month-old boy has seizures, developmental regression, hypotonia, and sparse, brittle, kinky hair. Serum copper and ceruloplasmin are low. Radiographs show metaphyseal abnormalities, and microscopy of hair shafts demonstrates pili torti.
lead: Deficiency of which cellular function most directly causes this disorder?
correct: ATP7A-mediated copper transport across cellular membranes
distractors: ATP7B-mediated biliary copper excretion from hepatocytes
Divalent metal transporter 1 uptake of dietary iron
distractor_notes: ATP7B dysfunction causes Wilson disease with impaired biliary copper excretion and copper accumulation rather than the systemic copper deficiency and kinky hair of Menkes disease.
Low ceruloplasmin is a consequence of disturbed copper homeostasis in Menkes disease; isolated ceruloplasmin deficiency is not the primary defect.
HFE participates in iron homeostasis, and pathogenic variants cause hereditary hemochromatosis rather than copper-deficiency neurodegeneration.
DMT1 transports divalent metals including iron at intestinal and endosomal membranes but is not the ATP7A defect responsible for Menkes disease.
key_expl: Menkes disease is an X-linked ATP7A-related copper transport disorder. ATP7A dysfunction prevents normal copper handling and delivery to copper-dependent enzymes, producing low serum copper/ceruloplasmin, neurodegeneration, connective-tissue abnormalities, and pili torti.
objective: Recognize Menkes disease and connect its neurologic, connective-tissue, and hair findings to defective ATP7A-mediated copper transport rather than ATP7B-mediated biliary copper excretion.

diagnosis: Length-time bias makes screening programs preferentially detect slower-growing disease with longer preclinical phases
mechanism: Screening is more likely to detect diseases that remain in a detectable preclinical state for a long time. Slowly progressive disease is therefore overrepresented among screen-detected cases, while rapidly progressive disease is more likely to become symptomatic between screening intervals. Apparent survival among screen-detected cases can consequently look better even without a true mortality benefit.
vignette: A cancer-screening program reports markedly longer survival after diagnosis among cancers detected by scheduled screening than among cancers presenting symptomatically. Subsequent analysis shows that screening disproportionately identifies indolent tumors with long preclinical detectable phases, whereas aggressive tumors often become symptomatic between screening visits.
lead: Which bias best explains the apparent survival advantage?
distractor_notes: Lead-time bias is an apparent increase in survival caused solely by diagnosing the same disease earlier in its natural history; this stem instead emphasizes preferential detection of biologically slower-growing tumors.
Recall bias arises from differential accuracy of remembered exposures and is not relevant to prospective screening detection.
Referral bias results when patterns of referral produce a nonrepresentative clinical sample; the mechanism described is differential detectability by disease growth rate.
Nondifferential exposure misclassification concerns similar measurement error across outcome groups and does not explain preferential detection of indolent disease.
key_expl: This is length-time bias: slowly growing tumors spend more time in a screen-detectable preclinical phase and are therefore overrepresented among screen-detected cases. Their intrinsically better prognosis can create an apparent screening benefit even when disease-specific mortality is unchanged.
objective: Differentiate length-time bias from lead-time bias by recognizing preferential screening detection of indolent disease with long preclinical detectable phases.
